title: ffreis flag registry
description: One declarative registry of every deliberate point of variation in a project. The dev toolbar, the runtime feature-flag resolver, and the compile-time build config are all GENERATED projections of this file — never hand-edited per feature. A port (mock<->real swap) is just kind:adapter; feature flags are the whole registry. Canonical source of truth. Spec: .claude/workspace/AGENTS.md § 'Every point of variation is a declared flag'. category:quality extends the same mechanism from infrastructure variation to component/media QUALITY rules (see flags/quality-rules.md): maximum rigor is the default and every opt-out is a declared, reasoned `exceptions` entry rather than a silent gap. Semantic conformance beyond this schema is enforced by scripts/validate-flag-registry.py.

$schema.description: Points at this schema so editors validate the registry as you type. Permitted explicitly because `additionalProperties` is false — without this property the documented consumer snippet would be rejected by the schema it names.

name.description: Stable snake_case identifier. Storage suffix: dev.route.<category>.<name>.

kind.description: adapter=swap implementation (mock<->real, testability); service=route among downstreams; value=typed config; gate=enable/disable a feature.

category.description: Toolbar grouping. data/api/model/content/lang are the 5 canonical dials; feature=pure gates; infra=deploy-time wiring; quality=a component/media quality rule (images, text/fonts, structure, accessibility) rather than a runtime dial — it never appears in the dev toolbar and is enforced at build time. A quality entry additionally requires `rule`, and must either name the gate that enforces it in `seam` or carry a reasoned `exceptions` entry saying why it does not enforce.

binding.description: compile=baked into the build (toolbar shows read-only); runtime=flippable live.

effect.description: route=pick among >=2 options; toggle=on/off. gate flags are always toggle.

options.description: Ordered least-real -> most-real for route flags (e.g. [mock, seeded, live]). Omit for toggle/value.

value_type.description: For kind:value — the type of the tunable. Omit for adapter/service/gate.

default.description: Cost/safety-guarded default. Model flags MUST default to the mock/cheapest option unless justified.

seam.description: The ONE code location where this flag is read. Invariant: one flag -> one seam. Absent only for pure build-input compile flags.

scope.description: env=per-environment default; session=dev localStorage/toolbar; user=per-user rollout; global=remote kill-switch.

cost_guard.description: True if flipping away from default can incur real cost (bill Bedrock, hit prod SES). Forces default=cheapest + a toolbar confirmation.

rule.description: For category:quality — the quality rule this entry governs, from the controlled vocabulary in flags/quality-rules.md. A rule id not listed there is rejected, so a typo cannot masquerade as a declared rule.

output_target.description: For category:quality — which output-target class(es) the rule governs. browser-live=a page a user interacts with in a browser (viewport, fold position and deferred loading all exist); document-export=a batch artifact with no runtime (PDF/Markdown/exported HTML file); raster-export=a batch image. A rule is meaningless outside the classes it names — lazy-loading has no meaning for a PNG, because there is no 'later' to defer to. Omit to mean every target this project produces.

exceptions.description: Declared, reasoned opt-outs. The point of the mechanism: an exception is a first-class visible allow-list entry, never a silent gap. An entry with no real reason is rejected by scripts/validate-flag-registry.py.

scope.description: What the exception covers — a path, a component, a named output target, or a stated condition. Narrow enough that a reader can tell whether a given case falls under it.

reason.description: WHY the rule does not apply here. A real engineering reason, not a restatement of the scope and not a placeholder — 'TODO'/'N/A'/'later' are rejected by the validator.

added.description: ISO date the exception was granted, so a reader can tell a deliberate long-standing carve-out from fresh debt.
